commands.name: batch-monitors
commands.description:
Batch Action on Monitors
Perform a batch action on monitors matching the provided filters.

Supported actions:
- **delete**: Permanently remove matching monitors
- **pause**: Pause matching monitors
- **unpause**: Unpause matching monitors

Use `dry_run: true` (the default) to preview which monitors would be affected before performing the action. Results are paginated via the `limit` parameter; loop until `has_more` is `false` to process all matching monitors.

options.name: --action
options.description: The action to perform on matching monitors. `delete` permanently removes them, `pause` sets their status to paused, and `unpause` sets their status to active.

options.name: --filter
options.description: At least one filter field must be provided to prevent accidental bulk operations.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: When `true`, returns the monitors that would be affected without performing the action. Defaults to `true`. Specify true/false; presence alone implies true; omit to inherit.

options.name: --limit
options.description: Maximum number of monitors to process in a single request. Defaults to 50, maximum 500.

options.name: --input
options.description: Load request JSON from a file path, '-' for stdin, or an inline JSON object/array string.

options.name: --request-json
options.description: Request body as JSON.

options.name: --request-file
options.description: Path to a JSON request file, or '-' for stdin.

commands.name: create-monitor
commands.description:
Create a Monitor
Creates a new Monitor to run recurring Exa searches on a schedule.

Monitors automatically execute your search query on a recurring schedule and deliver results to your webhook endpoint with automatic deduplication:

- **Date-based filtering** only fetches content since the last run

- **Semantic deduplication** tracks previous outputs to surface only new developments

The response includes a `webhookSecret` that is only returned once at creation time. Store it securely for webhook signature verification.

options.name: --name
options.description: An optional name for the monitor

options.name: --output-schema
options.description: Controls the format of the run output. Defaults to `{ "type": "text" }` if not specified. When `type` is `"text"`, the output is a plain text summary. When `type` is `"object"`, the output is structured JSON. If no `properties` are specified with `"object"` type, a schema is inferred automatically; otherwise the output adheres to the provided schema.

options.name: --metadata
options.description: Optional key-value metadata. Echoed back in webhook deliveries so you can route updates to systems like Slack.

options.name: --webhook-url
options.description: Webhook target URL.

options.name: --webhook-event
options.description: Repeatable event name. Allowed values: monitor.created, monitor.updated, monitor.deleted, monitor.run.created, monitor.run.completed.

commands.name: create
commands.description:
Create a Monitor
Creates a new `Monitor` to continuously keep your Websets updated with fresh data.

Monitors automatically run on your defined schedule to ensure your Websets stay current without manual intervention:

- **Find new content**: Execute `search` operations to discover fresh items matching your criteria
- **Update existing content**: Run `refresh` operations to update items contents and enrichments
- **Automated scheduling**: Configure `cron` expressions and `timezone` for precise scheduling control

options.description:
Entity the search will return results for.
It is not required to provide it, we automatically detect the entity from all the information provided in the query. Only use this when you need more fine control.

options.name: --criteria
options.description:
Criteria every item is evaluated against.
It's not required to provide your own criteria, we automatically detect the criteria from all the information provided in the query. Only use this when you need more fine control.

options.name: --max-people-per-company
options.description: Optional soft cap for people searches. When set, the search will try to include at most this many matching people from the same current employer company.

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Sources (existing imports or websets) to exclude from search results. Any results found within these sources will be omitted to prevent finding them during search.

options.name: --scope
options.description: Limit the search to specific sources (existing imports). Any results found within these sources matching the search criteria will be included in the Webset.

options.name: --recall
options.description:

Result of the analysis will be available in the `recall` field within the search request. Specify true/false; presence alone implies true; omit to inherit.

options.name: --behavior
options.description:

- **override**: Replace existing items and evaluate all items against new criteria
- **append**: Add new items to existing ones, keeping items that match the new criteria
